content:
Congruence is the first chapter where Class 7 students write PROOFS. It is also where the IMO checks a famous fact: AAA is NOT enough. Corresponding parts, in the right order, are everything. The free IMO Class 7 Congruence of Triangles online test below has 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Treat it as a diagnostic. Every explanation tells you what to revise.

What the IMO asks from Congruence of Triangles in Class 7

  • Congruence criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS.
  • Matching corresponding parts (CPCT).
  • Reading congruence statements like ΔXYZ ≅ ΔPQR.
  • Why AAA and SSA fail.
  • Simple two-step congruence arguments.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • ΔXYZ ≅ ΔPQR means X↔P, Y↔Q, Z↔R — the ORDER carries the information.
  • SAS needs the angle BETWEEN the two sides — an angle elsewhere proves nothing.
  • AAA gives the same SHAPE (similar), not the same SIZE.
  • RHS works only in right triangles: hypotenuse + one side.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Using SSA as if it were a valid test.
  • Reading corresponding parts from the figure instead of the congruence statement.
  • Forgetting the included-angle condition in SAS.

quiz.title: IMO Class 7 Congruence of Triangles Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 7: Congruence of Triangles

questions.q: Two figures are congruent when they have:
options: the same shape AND the same size
questions.explanation: Congruent figures cover each other exactly. Same shape alone gives similarity; congruence also needs equal size.

questions.q: ΔABC has AB = 8, BC = 10, AC = 6; ΔDEF has DE = 6, EF = 8, DF = 10. They are congruent by:
questions.explanation: AB = EF = 8, BC = DF = 10, AC = DE = 6. SSS.

questions.q: ΔABC and ΔDEF have AB = DE = 5, BC = EF = 6 and ∠ABC = ∠DEF = 70°. The criterion is:
questions.explanation: ∠B is included between AB and BC. SAS.

questions.q: The ASA criterion needs two angles and:
questions.explanation: The side must lie between the two angles. If the side is non-included, the criterion is AAS instead.

questions.q: Right triangles PQR and STU have ∠Q = ∠T = 90°, PQ = ST = 6 cm and hypotenuses PR = SU = 10 cm. The remaining sides QR and TU equal:
questions.explanation: √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8. Both triangles have third side 8 cm — congruent by RHS.

questions.q: E, F are midpoints of the equal sides AB, AC of isosceles ΔABC. ΔBEC ≅ ΔCFB by:
questions.explanation: BE = CF (halves of equal sides), ∠EBC = ∠FCB (base angles), BC common. SAS — so the "cross" segments CE and BF are equal.

questions.q: In square ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD are equal because ΔABC ≅ ΔBAD by:
questions.explanation: AB = BA, BC = AD, and the included right angles ∠B = ∠A. SAS, so AC = BD by CPCT.

questions.q: A square has how many lines of symmetry?
questions.explanation: Two diagonals + horizontal and vertical mid-lines. 4 lines.

questions.q: The order of rotational symmetry of a square is:
All 8 lines of symmetry of a regular octagon are drawn. The octagon is divided into congruent right triangles numbering:
questions.explanation: The 8 mirror lines through the centre create 16 sectors. Each is a right triangle with central angle 22.5°.
